items.section_title: 3.8 · Objective j — Heredity and carcinogenesis
items.html: Protooncogene mutation. Mutation converts a protooncogene into an oncogene, which encodes oncoproteins that promote continued growth in an uncontrolled manner.
cites: Abnormal Cell Growth for posting.pptx, Slide 29

src.question: What happens when a protooncogene mutates?
src.key: It becomes an oncogene, which encodes oncoproteins that promote continued uncontrolled growth
src.explanation: Correct — mutation converts a protooncogene to an oncogene, whose oncoproteins promote continued growth in an uncontrolled manner.

items.section_title: 3.6 · Objectives g & h — Gene alterations and chemical carcinogenesis
items.html: Genes for self-destruction of damaged cells. Genes promoting apoptosis of cells with damaged deoxyribonucleic acid stop the damage becoming permanent in dividing cells, preventing a mutation being carried on into the daughter cells.
cites: Abnormal Cell Growth for posting.pptx, Slide 30

src.question: Why are genes promoting self destruction of cells with damaged deoxyribonucleic acid necessary?
src.key: To stop the damage becoming permanent in dividing cells
src.explanation: Correct — apoptosis prevents a mutation being carried on into the daughter cells.

items.section_title: 3.3 · Objectives c & k — Neoplasia and histological grading
items.html: Steps in invasion. Besides invasion into adjacent structures, abnormal cell-substratum interaction is a step in invasion, as the cell's relationship with its own supporting matrix changes.
cites: Abnormal Cell Growth for posting.pptx, Slide 24

src.question: Besides invasion into adjacent structures, which abnormal interaction is a step in invasion?
src.key: Abnormal cell-substratum interaction
src.explanation: Correct — the cell's relationship with its own supporting matrix changes.

items.section_title: 3.5 · Objectives e & f — Classifying tumors by origin
items.html: Adenoma function. An adenoma can sometimes secrete the hormone or hormones produced by its gland of origin, because the tumor retains a function of the tissue it came from.
cites: Abnormal Cell Growth for posting.pptx, Slide 16

src.question: What can an adenoma sometimes do that reflects its origin?
src.key: Secrete the hormone or hormones produced by its gland of origin
src.explanation: Correct — the tumor retains a function of the tissue it came from.

items.section_title: 3.3 · Objectives c & k — Neoplasia and histological grading
items.html: Tumor cell versus normal cell. Compared with normal cells, tumor cells show abnormal regulation of cell growth and abnormal cell-cell interactions.
cites: Abnormal Cell Growth for posting.pptx, Slide 19

src.question: Which two abnormalities separate a tumor cell from a normal cell?
src.key: Abnormal regulation of cell growth, and abnormal cell-cell interactions
src.explanation: Correct — compared with normal cells, tumor cells show abnormal regulation of cell growth and abnormal cell-cell interactions.

items.section_title: 3.4 · Objective d — Routes of tumor spread
items.html: Hematogenous spread of cancer. Hematogenous spread is typically venous, so fragments in the portal vein reach the liver and those in the inferior vena cava reach the lungs, because those are the organs each vein drains into.
cites: Abnormal Cell Growth for posting.pptx, Slide 14

src.question: Why do cancers spreading through the portal vein and the inferior vena cava reach the liver and the lungs?
src.key: Because those are the organs each vein drains into
src.explanation: Correct — hematogenous spread is typically venous, so fragments in the portal vein reach the liver and those in the inferior vena cava reach the lungs.

items.section_title: 4.2 · Objectives d & e — Globe shape, and the age-related conditions
items.html: Myopia. Myopia is nearsightedness, so a myopic patient sees objects up close well.

src.question: What can a myopic patient see well?
src.key: Objects up close
src.explanation: Correct — myopia is nearsightedness, so near vision is the preserved one.

items.section_title: 4.2 · Objectives d & e — Globe shape, and the age-related conditions
items.html: Conjunctival fornix. The fornix is the flexible junctional cul-de-sac where palpebral and bulbar conjunctiva meet, and its slack permits free rotation of the globe.

src.question: What is the conjunctival fornix?
src.key: A flexible junctional cul-de-sac that permits free rotation of the globe
src.explanation: Correct — the fornix is the flexible junctional cul-de-sac where palpebral and bulbar conjunctiva meet, and its slack permits free rotation of the globe.

items.section_title: 5.5 · Otitis media and otitis externa
items.html: Protection of the outer ear canal. The outer third of the ear canal is protected by cerumen from ceruminous glands and by hair follicles.

src.question: What protects the outer third of the ear canal?
src.key: Cerumen from ceruminous glands, and hair follicles
src.explanation: Ceruminous glands produce protective cerumen, and the outer third of the canal also has protective hair follicles.

items.section_title: 5.1 · Objectives 1 & 3 — Anatomy and auditory transduction
items.html: Chalazion. A chalazion is a non-tender, sterile lipogranuloma of a blocked meibomian gland; being sterile and granulomatous is what separates it from an infection.

src.question: Which description fits a chalazion?
src.key: A non-tender, sterile lipogranuloma of a blocked meibomian gland
src.explanation: Correct — sterile and granulomatous is what separates it from an infection.

items.section_title: 5.5 · Otitis media and otitis externa
items.html: Fungal otitis externa. Prolonged antibiotic use suppresses the bacteria, and Aspergillus niger or Candida albicans then take over as fungal otitis externa.

src.question: Why does prolonged antibiotic use predispose to FUNGAL otitis externa?
src.key: It removes competing bacteria
src.explanation: Prolonged antibiotic use suppresses the bacteria, and Aspergillus niger or Candida albicans then take over as fungal otitis externa.

items.section_title: 1.4 · Objective c — Mechanism of white blood cells
items.html: Monocyte role in immunity. After phagocytosis, monocytes present pieces of pathogens to T cells so that the pathogens may be recognized again and killed.

src.question: Beyond phagocytosis, what is the monocyte's role in the immune response?
src.key: Presenting pathogen pieces to T cells so it can be recognized again and killed
src.explanation: After phagocytosis, monocytes present pieces of pathogens to T cells so that the pathogens may be recognized again and killed.

items.section_title: 5.2 · Objective 5 — Conductive against sensorineural loss
items.html: Dacryoadenitis. Dacryoadenitis is inflammation or infection of the lacrimal gland, causing superotemporal orbital rim pain and an S-shaped lid deformity.

src.question: Which lid deformity goes with dacryoadenitis?
src.key: An S-shaped lid deformity
src.explanation: Correct — dacryoadenitis is inflammation or infection of the lacrimal gland, causing superotemporal orbital rim pain and an S-shaped lid deformity.

items.section_title: 4.2 · Objectives d & e — Globe shape, and the age-related conditions
items.html: Hyperopia. Hyperopia is farsightedness, so a hyperopic patient sees objects far away well.

src.question: What can a hyperopic patient see well?
src.key: Objects far away
src.explanation: Correct — hyperopia is farsightedness, so distance vision is the preserved one.

items.section_title: 5.5 · Otitis media and otitis externa
items.html: Episcleritis. Inflammation of the superficial episclera is a self-limiting blush with no severe pain and no threat to vision, unlike the deep, emergency inflammation of scleritis.

src.question: How is episcleritis best characterized?
src.key: A self-limiting inflammatory blush, not vision-threatening and without severe pain
src.explanation: Correct — inflammation of the superficial episclera is a self-limiting blush with no severe pain and no threat to vision, unlike the deep, emergency inflammation of scleritis.

items.section_title: 1.5 · Objective d — Vascular changes in acute inflammation
items.html: Stasis in acute inflammation. Hemoconcentration and stasis come immediately before leukocyte adhesion in the sequence of acute inflammation, since slowed flow lets leukocytes contact the endothelium.

src.question: Why does stasis of blood flow matter mechanistically in acute inflammation?
src.key: It precedes leukocyte adhesion, since slowed flow lets leukocytes contact the endothelium
src.explanation: Hemoconcentration and stasis sit immediately before leukocyte adhesion in the sequence of events of acute inflammation.

items.section_title: 4.4 · Objective f — Glaucoma
items.html: Optic disc cupping in glaucoma. Raised pressure compresses retinal ganglion cell axons, the cells die by apoptosis, and the cup widens to a cup-to-disc ratio greater than 0.5.

src.question: Above what cup-to-disc ratio is optic disc cupping progressive?
src.key: Greater than 0.5
src.explanation: Correct — raised pressure compresses retinal ganglion cell axons, the cells die by apoptosis, and the cup widens to a cup-to-disc ratio above 0.5.

items.section_title: 4.4 · Objective f — Glaucoma
items.html: Pterygium versus pinguecula. Both are fibrovascular proliferations from chronic ultraviolet, wind and dust exposure, but only a pterygium grows onto the cornea and can impair vision.

src.question: What single feature separates a pterygium from a pinguecula?
src.key: A pterygium grows onto the cornea; a pinguecula does not
src.explanation: Correct — both are fibrovascular proliferations from chronic ultraviolet, wind and dust exposure, but only the pterygium encroaches onto the cornea and can impair vision.

items.section_title: 5.2 · Objective 5 — Conductive against sensorineural loss
items.html: Cranial nerve VIII lesion versus cochlear damage. Both lie beyond the conducting chain, so both give sensorineural loss; the category is defined by where the defect sits, not by which structure failed.

src.question: Why does a lesion of cranial nerve VIII produce the same audiometric pattern as cochlear damage?
src.key: Both lie beyond the conducting chain
src.explanation: Both sit beyond the conducting chain, so both give sensorineural loss. The category is defined by where the defect sits, not by which of the two structures failed.

items.section_title: 4.5 · Objectives h & i — Retinal detachment and macular degeneration
items.html: Subconjunctival hemorrhage. Blood leaked from ruptured episcleral or conjunctival capillaries lies beneath the conjunctiva; it is benign and clears in one to two weeks, changing color like a bruise.

src.question: What is the natural course of a subconjunctival hemorrhage?
src.key: Benign, resolving over one to two weeks with bruise-like color changes
src.explanation: Correct — blood leaked from ruptured episcleral or conjunctival capillaries lies beneath the conjunctiva and clears in one to two weeks, changing color like a bruise.

items.section_title: 5.5 · Otitis media and otitis externa
items.html: Keratitis. Contact lens wearers carry a Pseudomonas risk. Keratitis is an emergency because it can progress to stromal ulceration, perforation and endophthalmitis.

src.question: Which pairing of patient group and organism carries particular risk in keratitis?
src.key: Contact lens wearers, from Pseudomonas
src.explanation: Correct — contact lens wearers carry a Pseudomonas risk, and keratitis is an emergency because it can progress to stromal ulceration, perforation and endophthalmitis.

items.section_title: 4.2 · Objectives d & e — Globe shape, and the age-related conditions
items.html: Presbyopia. The sclerotic lens and ciliary muscle can no longer accommodate, so near objects cannot be focused and reading glasses or bifocals are needed.

src.question: What is the functional consequence of presbyopia?
src.key: Inability to focus on near objects, so reading glasses are needed
src.explanation: Correct — the sclerotic lens and ciliary muscle can no longer accommodate, so near objects cannot be focused and readers or bifocals are needed.

items.section_title: 5.5 · Otitis media and otitis externa
items.html: Tympanic membrane. The tympanic membrane separates the external ear from the middle ear and is the first moving part of the conducting chain, vibrating the ossicles; perforating it causes conductive loss.

src.question: Which structure separates the external ear from the middle ear?
src.key: The tympanic membrane, which vibrates the ossicles
src.explanation: It is the boundary and the first moving part of the conducting chain, which is why perforating it causes conductive loss.

items.section_title: 5.1 · Objectives 1 & 3 — Anatomy and auditory transduction
items.html: Herpes simplex epithelial keratitis. The classical lesion is a branching dendritic corneal ulcer whose tips end in terminal bulbs on fluorescein stain.

src.question: What is the classical corneal finding in herpes simplex epithelial keratitis?
src.key: A dendritic ulcer with terminal bulbs on fluorescein staining
src.explanation: Correct — the classical herpes simplex epithelial keratitis lesion is a branching dendritic corneal ulcer whose tips end in terminal bulbs on fluorescein stain.

items.section_title: 4.6 · Objective j — Visual field deficits by lesion site
items.html: Orbital versus periorbital cellulitis. In orbital cellulitis, bacteria breach the orbital septum into the soft tissue behind the globe, and purulence there causes proptosis, reduced extraocular movement and risk of optic nerve compression.

src.question: Which findings does orbital cellulitis show that periorbital cellulitis lacks?
src.key: Proptosis, reduced eye movement and risk of optic nerve compression
src.explanation: Correct — bacteria breach the orbital septum into the soft tissue behind the globe, and the purulence there causes proptosis, reduced extraocular movement and optic nerve compression risk.

items.section_title: 4.1 · Objectives a & b — Anatomy and the physiology of vision
items.html: Outermost ocular structures. The lids, cornea and conjunctiva are outer, easily visible structures that face the environment directly, so they are more susceptible to infection, trauma and environmental change.

src.question: What do the lids, cornea and conjunctiva have in common as the outermost ocular structures?
src.key: They are more susceptible to infection, trauma and environmental change
src.explanation: Correct — as the outer, easily visible structures, the lids, cornea and conjunctiva face the environment directly and are more susceptible to infection, trauma and environmental change.

items.section_title: 5.5 · Otitis media and otitis externa
items.html: Scleritis. Scleritis is an emergency of the deep sclera with boring pain and a risk of scleral melting, strongly linked to rheumatoid arthritis, granulomatosis with polyangiitis and systemic vasculitis.

src.question: Which systemic diseases are strongly linked to scleritis?
src.key: Rheumatoid arthritis, granulomatosis with polyangiitis and systemic vasculitis
src.explanation: Correct — scleritis, an emergency of the deep sclera with boring pain and a risk of scleral melting, is strongly linked to rheumatoid arthritis, granulomatosis with polyangiitis and systemic vasculitis.

items.section_title: 2.2 · Objective b — Primary skin lesions
items.html: Causes of bullae. Bullae result from mechanical factors, infections, toxins, chemicals and autoimmunity, with bullous impetigo the bacterial example and bullous pemphigoid the autoimmune one.

src.question: Which factors cause bullae?
src.key: Mechanical factors, infections, toxins, chemicals and autoimmunity
src.explanation: with bullous impetigo as the bacterial example and bullous pemphigoid as the autoimmune one.

items.section_title: 1.4 · Objective c — Mechanism of white blood cells
items.html: Fate of monocytes. Monocytes eventually leave the bloodstream to become tissue macrophages, which clear debris and attack microorganisms.

src.question: What is the fate of a monocyte once it leaves the bloodstream?
src.key: A tissue macrophage that clears debris and attacks microorganisms
src.explanation: Monocytes eventually leave the bloodstream to become tissue macrophages with exactly these roles.

items.section_title: 4.2 · Objectives d & e — Globe shape, and the age-related conditions
items.html: Lipid layer of the tear film. Meibomian glands in the tarsal plates produce the lipid layer, which prevents evaporation; when they are obstructed, as in blepharitis, tears evaporate excessively.

src.question: What does the lipid layer of the tear film do?
src.key: It prevents evaporation
src.explanation: Correct — meibomian glands in the tarsal plates produce the lipid layer, which prevents evaporation; when they are obstructed, as in blepharitis, tears evaporate excessively.

items.section_title: 5.2 · Objective 5 — Conductive against sensorineural loss
items.html: Hypopyon. A hypopyon is a collection of pus in the anterior chamber, the inflammatory layer seen in the front of a severely inflamed eye.

src.question: What is a hypopyon?
src.key: Pus in the anterior chamber
src.explanation: Correct — a hypopyon is a collection of pus in the anterior chamber, the inflammatory layer seen in the front of a severely inflamed eye.

items.section_title: 4.1 · Objectives a & b — Anatomy and the physiology of vision
items.html: Panophthalmitis versus endophthalmitis. Panophthalmitis involves every layer of the globe and can spread into the orbit, beyond the intraocular infection of endophthalmitis.

src.question: How does panophthalmitis differ from endophthalmitis?
src.key: It involves every layer of the globe and may enter the orbit
src.explanation: Correct — pan- means all: panophthalmitis involves every layer of the globe and can spread into the orbit, beyond the intraocular infection of endophthalmitis.

items.section_title: 1.1 · Objective a — Molecular mechanisms of inflammatory processes
items.html: Arteriolar vasodilation in inflammation. Vasodilation of the arterioles supplying an injured region increases blood flow to that region.

src.question: Vasodilation of the arterioles supplying an injured region produces which immediate effect?
src.key: Increased blood flow to the injured region
src.explanation: Vasodilation of the supplying arterioles increases blood flow.

items.section_title: 4.5 · Objectives h & i — Retinal detachment and macular degeneration
items.html: Diabetic retinopathy. Chronic hyperglycemia damages retinal capillaries, and diabetic retinopathy is the leading cause of new-onset blindness in United States adults aged twenty to seventy-four.

src.question: Diabetic retinopathy is the leading cause of new-onset blindness in which group?
src.key: United States adults aged twenty to seventy-four
src.explanation: Correct — chronic hyperglycemia damages retinal capillaries, and diabetic retinopathy is the leading cause of new-onset blindness in United States adults aged twenty to seventy-four.

items.section_title: 3.8 · Objective j — Heredity and carcinogenesis
items.html: Inherited tumor suppressor alteration in melanoma. p16, also called INK4a, is associated with malignant melanoma.
cites: Abnormal Cell Growth for posting.pptx, Slide 39

src.question: Which inherited tumor suppressor alteration is associated with malignant melanoma?
src.key: p16, also called INK4a
src.explanation: Correct — p16 (INK4a) is an inherited tumor suppressor alteration associated with malignant melanoma.

items.section_title: 3.8 · Objective j — Heredity and carcinogenesis
items.html: Xeroderma pigmentosum. Defective repair genes mean ultraviolet B damage cannot be repaired, raising the risk of skin cancer in sun-exposed areas; it is a repair-gene disease rather than a tumor suppressor one.
cites: Abnormal Cell Growth for posting.pptx, Slide 40

src.question: Which statement correctly describes the inherited defect in xeroderma pigmentosum?
src.key: Defective repair genes, so ultraviolet B damage cannot be repaired
src.explanation: Correct — the consequence is an increased risk of skin cancer in sun-exposed areas. It is a repair-gene disease rather than a tumor suppressor one.

items.section_title: 3.6 · Objectives g & h — Gene alterations and chemical carcinogenesis
items.html: Promoters. They drive proliferation of cells already damaged by an initiator; sustained or enhanced proliferation raises the risk of successive mutations leading to cancer.
cites: Abnormal Cell Growth for posting.pptx, Slide 31

src.question: What do promoters do?
src.key: They drive proliferation of cells already damaged by an initiator
src.explanation: Correct — sustained or enhanced proliferation raises the risk of successive mutations leading to cancer.

items.section_title: 5.5 · Otitis media and otitis externa
items.html: Eustachian tube dysfunction. The tube fails to open, so the mucosa absorbs the gases in the air-filled middle ear and the pressure falls; that negative pressure starts the otitis media sequence.

src.question: What is the sequence by which Eustachian tube dysfunction creates negative middle ear pressure?
src.key: The tube fails to open, so the mucosa absorbs the gases
src.explanation: The middle ear is an air-filled space; if it is not re-ventilated, the mucosa absorbs the gases and the pressure falls. That negative pressure is the start of the otitis media sequence.

items.section_title: 2.3 · Objective c — Secondary skin lesions
items.html: Secondary skin lesion. It is a modification or change of a primary lesion caused by infection, trauma or other factors, so it may or may not still resemble what it came from.

src.question: What defines a secondary skin lesion?
src.key: A modification or change of a primary lesion caused by infection, trauma or other factors
src.explanation: which is why a secondary lesion may or may not still resemble what it came from.

items.section_title: 1.4 · Objective c — Mechanism of white blood cells
items.html: B lymphocytes. They make antibodies, act as antigen-presenting cells and become memory B cells, driving the humoral immune response.

src.question: What do B lymphocytes do?
src.key: Making antibodies, presenting antigen, and becoming memory B cells
src.explanation: B lymphocytes make antibodies, act as antigen-presenting cells and become memory B cells; they drive the humoral immune response.

items.section_title: 4.2 · Objectives d & e — Globe shape, and the age-related conditions
items.html: Amblyopia. Reduced best-corrected acuity from abnormal visual development; it is a visual deficit rather than a mechanical one, as visual processing developed abnormally during the critical pediatric period.

src.question: What is amblyopia?
src.key: Reduced best-corrected acuity from abnormal visual development
src.explanation: Correct — amblyopia is a visual deficit rather than a mechanical one: best-corrected acuity stays reduced because visual processing developed abnormally during the critical pediatric period.

items.section_title: 5.1 · Objectives 1 & 3 — Anatomy and auditory transduction
items.html: External versus internal hordeolum. An external hordeolum is an acute abscess of the glands of Zeis or Moll at the lash follicles; an internal one involves a meibomian gland in the tarsal plate.

src.question: Which glands are involved in an external as opposed to an internal hordeolum?
src.key: External involves the glands of Zeis or Moll; internal involves a meibomian gland
src.explanation: Correct — an external hordeolum is an acute abscess of the Zeis or Moll glands at the lash follicles, and an internal one involves a meibomian gland in the tarsal plate.

items.section_title: 2.5 · Objective d — Molecular mechanisms of common conditions
items.html: Psoriasis mechanism. Active T cells in the epidermis drive keratinocyte proliferation and excess cytokines, such as tumor necrosis factor alpha, so skin cells multiply up to ten times faster.

src.question: Which mechanism drives psoriasis?
src.key: Active T cells in the epidermis drive keratinocyte proliferation and excess cytokines, such as tumor necrosis factor alpha
src.explanation: Active T cells infiltrate the epidermis, stimulating keratinocyte proliferation and excess cytokines (tumor necrosis factor alpha, interferon gamma and interleukin-12), so skin cells multiply up to ten times faster.

items.section_title: 2.5 · Objective d — Molecular mechanisms of common conditions
items.html: Petechiae, purpura and ecchymoses. All three are bleeding into the dermis with similar underlying pathology, differing by size: petechiae 1 to 2 millimeters or less, purpura 3 to 10 millimeters, ecchymoses greater than 10 millimeters.

src.question: How do petechiae, purpura and ecchymoses differ?
src.key: By size — petechiae 1 to 2 millimeters or less, purpura 3 to 10 millimeters, ecchymoses greater than 10 millimeters — with similar underlying pathology
src.explanation: All three are bleeding into the dermis with similar underlying pathology, separated by size, from pinpoint petechiae to ecchymoses over 10 millimeters.

items.section_title: 1.6 · Objective e — Cellular changes in acute inflammation
items.html: Opsonins. Recognition and attachment during phagocytosis are enhanced by serum factors known as opsonins, such as immunoglobulin G and complement fragment C3b.

src.question: Recognition and attachment during phagocytosis are enhanced by the presence of what?
src.key: Serum factors known as opsonins
src.explanation: Opsonins such as immunoglobulin G and complement fragment C3b enhance recognition and attachment during phagocytosis.

items.section_title: 5.8 · Rhinology
items.html: Nasal polyps. They are non-neoplastic: no new tissue grows; the mucosa is edematous, forming benign edematous masses of the mucous membranes of the sinus ostia or ethmoid air cells.

src.question: Why are nasal polyps classed as non-neoplastic?
src.key: No new tissue grows; the mucosa is edematous
src.explanation: Nasal polyps are benign edematous masses of the mucous membranes of the sinus ostia or ethmoid air cells, not new neoplastic tissue.

items.section_title: 5.2 · Objective 5 — Conductive against sensorineural loss
items.html: Cerumen impaction. It causes conductive rather than sensorineural loss because it blocks sound delivery down the canal; the cochlea is untouched and the defect is purely one of delivery.

src.question: Why does cerumen impaction cause conductive rather than sensorineural loss?
src.key: It blocks sound delivery down the canal
src.explanation: The cochlea is untouched, and the defect is purely one of delivery.

items.section_title: 1.4 · Objective c — Mechanism of white blood cells
items.html: Eosinophils. Cells with bi-lobed nuclei and pink-orange granules are eosinophils, which predominate in allergic reactions and parasitic infections, so such an infiltrate suggests an allergic or parasitic process.

src.question: A patient's inflamed tissue shows a leukocyte infiltrate dominated by cells with bi-lobed nuclei and pink-orange granules. Which process does this pattern most suggest?
src.key: An allergic or parasitic process
src.explanation: Bi-lobed nuclei with pink-orange granules identify eosinophils, which predominate in allergic reactions and parasitic infections.

items.section_title: 2.5 · Objective d — Molecular mechanisms of common conditions
items.html: Petechiae. Minor bleeding into the dermis, such as from capillary rupture, gives non-blanchable pinpoint deposits of blood 1 to 2 millimeters or less; other causes include infection, thrombocytopenia or vasculitis.

src.question: Which description of petechiae is accurate?
src.key: Minor bleeding into the dermis, such as from capillary rupture, 1 to 2 millimeters or less
src.explanation: Petechiae are non-blanchable pinpoint deposits of blood in the dermis, 1 to 2 millimeters or less, from minor bleeding such as capillary rupture, infection, thrombocytopenia or vasculitis.

items.section_title: 5.6 · Objective 4 — Equilibrium, and vertigo against dizziness
items.html: Vertigo from asymmetrical vestibular input. Balance is a comparison, so unequal input is indistinguishable from turning: the brain reads the mismatch as motion.

src.question: Why does asymmetrical vestibular input produce a false sense of motion?
src.key: The brain reads the mismatch as motion
src.explanation: Balance is a comparison, so unequal input is indistinguishable from turning.

items.section_title: 5.9 · Larynx and neck
items.html: Matted lymph nodes. They have lost their individual capsules and move together as one mass; persistent rubbery or matted nodes in older adults require assessment to rule out lymphoma.

src.question: What does it mean, structurally, for lymph nodes to be MATTED?
src.key: They move together as one mass
src.explanation: Matted nodes have lost their individual capsules and move together as one mass, and persistent rubbery or matted nodes in older adults require assessment to rule out lymphoma.

items.section_title: 4.4 · Objective f — Glaucoma
items.html: Iris bombé. Forward displacement of the iris against the cornea; in angle closure, pupil dilation pushes the iris forward and blocks aqueous outflow totally so pressure spikes.

src.question: What is iris bombé?
src.key: Forward displacement of the iris against the cornea
src.explanation: Correct — in angle closure, pupil dilation pushes the iris forward against the cornea, and this iris bombé blocks aqueous outflow totally so pressure spikes.

items.section_title: 1.7 · Objective f — Mediators of inflammation and their functions
items.html: Histamine. It is the first mediator of the inflammatory response, dilating arterioles and increasing capillary and venule permeability.

src.question: Which statement about histamine in the inflammatory response is correct?
src.key: The first mediator of the response, dilating arterioles and increasing capillary and venule permeability
src.explanation: Histamine is the first mediator of the initial response, dilating arterioles and increasing capillary and venule permeability.

items.section_title: 2.5 · Objective d — Molecular mechanisms of common conditions
items.html: Actinic keratosis. The most common precancer, arising on skin damaged by chronic ultraviolet exposure: cumulative ultraviolet damage causes intraepidermal proliferation of dysplastic keratinocytes, raising squamous cell carcinoma risk.

src.question: Which description of actinic keratosis is accurate?
src.key: Cumulative ultraviolet damage causing intraepidermal proliferation of dysplastic keratinocytes, raising squamous cell carcinoma risk
src.explanation: Actinic keratosis is the most common precancer, arising on skin damaged by chronic ultraviolet exposure, and it carries a higher risk of squamous cell carcinoma.

items.section_title: 2.3 · Objective c — Secondary skin lesions
items.html: Scarring in ulcers versus erosions. An ulcer destroys dermal collagen, which healing must replace, so it scars; an erosion spares the dermis, and scarring is a dermal repair process.

src.question: Why does an ulcer scar while an erosion generally does not?
src.key: An ulcer destroys dermal collagen, which healing must replace; an erosion spares the dermis
src.explanation: Scarring is a dermal repair process, so a lesion confined above the junction has nothing to scar.

items.section_title: 1.1 · Objective a — Molecular mechanisms of inflammatory processes
items.html: Exudation. Endothelial contraction increasing capillary permeability allows fluid and blood proteins to enter the interstitium.

src.question: Which vascular change is directly responsible for allowing fluid and blood proteins to enter the interstitium?
src.key: Endothelial contraction increasing capillary permeability
src.explanation: Endothelial contraction is what allows the increased permeability through which exudation occurs.

items.section_title: 2.3 · Objective c — Secondary skin lesions
items.html: Scale. A compact portion of desquamating stratum corneum, varying in size and thickness; psoriasis is an example.

src.question: What tissue makes up a scale?
src.key: A compact portion of desquamating stratum corneum, varying in size and thickness
src.explanation: A scale is a compact portion of desquamating stratum corneum that varies in size and thickness, and psoriasis is an example.

items.section_title: 5.4 · Ototoxicity and noise
items.html: Presbycusis. High frequencies go first, taking the speech consonants such as /s/, /f/ and /t/, which makes voices hard to discriminate in noisy environments.

src.question: Why does presbycusis make voices hard to discriminate in noisy environments?
src.key: High frequencies go first, taking the speech consonants
src.explanation: Presbycusis begins with high-frequency tones, which include speech consonants such as /s/, /f/ and /t/, making voice discrimination difficult in noisy environments.

items.section_title: 2.2 · Objective b — Primary skin lesions
items.html: Vesicle versus bulla. A vesicle is up to 5 millimeters, with fluid within or beneath the epidermis; a bulla is larger (greater than 5 millimeters) and separates epidermis from dermis, a deeper plane of cleavage.

src.question: What distinguishes a vesicle from a bulla?
src.key: A vesicle is up to 5 millimeters, with fluid within or beneath the epidermis; a bulla is larger and separates epidermis from dermis
src.explanation: A vesicle holds fluid containing inflammatory cells within or directly beneath the epidermis; a bulla, greater than 5 millimeters, involves separation of epidermis from dermis. The bulla represents a deeper plane of cleavage, not merely a bigger blister.

items.section_title: 2.1 · Objective a — Anatomy of the integumentary system
items.html: Stratum spinosum. Also called the prickle cell layer: its 8 to 10 keratinocyte layers are connected by intercellular connections called desmosomes, which form a spiny appearance.

src.question: What gives the spinous layer its alternative name of prickle cell layer?
src.key: Keratinocytes connected by intercellular connections called desmosomes, which form a spiny appearance
src.explanation: The 8 to 10 keratinocyte layers of the stratum spinosum are joined by desmosomes, which give the spiny look behind the name prickle cell layer.

items.section_title: 2.2 · Objective b — Primary skin lesions
items.html: Hypopigmented versus hyperpigmented macules. Vitiligo reflects loss of melanocytes, whereas hyperpigmented macules (ephelides, café au lait spots, Mongolian spots) reflect increased melanin production in the basal layer of the epidermis.

src.question: How does the mechanism of a hypopigmented macule such as vitiligo differ from that of a hyperpigmented macule?
src.key: Loss of melanocytes, against increased melanin production in the basal layer of the epidermis
src.explanation: Vitiligo reflects loss of melanocytes, while hyperpigmented macules such as ephelides, café au lait spots and Mongolian spots reflect increased basal melanin.

items.section_title: 1.3 · Objective b — Patterns of inflammation
items.html: Hemorrhagic inflammation. It is caused by damage to blood vessels and occurs together with other exudates.

src.question: Which combination of cause and relationship to other exudates characterizes hemorrhagic inflammation?
src.key: Damage to blood vessels, and occurring together with other exudates
src.explanation: Hemorrhagic inflammation is damage to blood vessels occurring with other exudates.

items.section_title: 2.6 · Objective d — Skin cancers
items.html: Melanoma growth phases. Radial growth in the epidermis, then vertical growth into the dermis, thickening, then lymphatic and vascular invasion.

src.question: What are the growth phases of melanoma, in order?
src.key: Radial growth in the epidermis, vertical growth into the dermis, thickening, then lymphatic and vascular invasion
src.explanation: Melanoma cells first multiply within the epidermis, then penetrate the dermis, grow deeper and thicker, and finally invade lymphatics and blood vessels.

items.section_title: 2.3 · Objective c — Secondary skin lesions
items.html: Erosion versus ulcer. An erosion stays above the dermal-epidermal junction; an ulcer loses epidermis AND dermis, destroying collagen with inflammatory infiltrate.

src.question: What is the tissue distinction between an erosion and an ulcer?
src.key: An erosion stays above the dermal-epidermal junction; an ulcer loses epidermis AND dermis, destroying collagen with inflammatory infiltrate
src.explanation: The junction is the boundary that separates them, and crossing it is what brings collagen destruction into play.

items.section_title: 5.7 · The four peripheral vertigos
items.html: Labyrinthitis. It impairs hearing AND balance together because inflammation spans both the semicircular canals and the cochlea, through inflammatory swelling, vascular congestion and endolymphatic disruption.

src.question: Why does labyrinthitis impair hearing AND balance together?
src.key: Inflammation across both the semicircular canals and the cochlea
src.explanation: Inflammatory swelling, vascular congestion and endolymphatic disruption affect the semicircular canals and the cochlea at once, impairing balance and the organ of Corti together.

items.section_title: 2.5 · Objective d — Molecular mechanisms of common conditions
items.html: Psoriasis epidermal changes. Epidermal hyperplasia (active T cells drive keratinocyte proliferation), loss of the stratum granulosum, and failed lipid secretion causing xeroderma.

src.question: Which structural epidermal changes occur in psoriasis?
src.key: Epidermal hyperplasia, loss of the stratum granulosum, and failed lipid secretion causing xeroderma
src.explanation: Active T cells drive keratinocyte proliferation into epidermal hyperplasia, the stratum granulosum is lost, and epidermal cells stop secreting lipids.

items.section_title: 1.4 · Objective c — Mechanism of white blood cells
items.html: Regulatory (suppressor) T cells. They return immunity to normal after infection and prevent autoimmunity.

src.question: What do regulatory (suppressor) T cells do?
src.key: Returning immunity to normal after infection, and preventing autoimmunity
src.explanation: Regulatory (suppressor) T cells return the immune system to normal operation after infection and prevent autoimmunity.

items.section_title: 5.2 · Objective 5 — Conductive against sensorineural loss
items.html: Conductive hearing loss. Weber lateralizes to the AFFECTED ear and Rinne is abnormal, with bone conduction greater than air.

src.question: Which pair of tuning fork findings indicates conductive hearing loss?
src.key: Weber to the AFFECTED ear; Rinne shows bone conduction greater than air
src.explanation: With sound wave transmission to the oval window defective, Weber lateralizes to the AFFECTED ear and Rinne is abnormal, with bone conduction greater than air.

items.section_title: 2.2 · Objective b — Primary skin lesions
items.html: Primary versus secondary skin lesions. A primary lesion is the direct result of the underlying disease and retains its original unmodified appearance; a secondary lesion has been modified over time and may or may not still resemble the original.

src.question: What distinguishes a primary from a secondary skin lesion?
src.key: A primary lesion is the direct result of the underlying disease and retains its original unmodified appearance; a secondary lesion has been modified over time
src.explanation: and a secondary lesion may or may not still resemble the lesion it came from.

items.section_title: 2.5 · Objective d — Molecular mechanisms of common conditions
items.html: Seborrheic dermatitis. The cause is incompletely understood, but microbiome dysbiosis, altered immunity and barrier dysfunction contribute, in the sebaceous-rich scalp, face and upper trunk.

src.question: Which description of seborrheic dermatitis is accurate?
src.key: Microbiome dysbiosis, altered immunity and barrier dysfunction, in the sebaceous-rich scalp, face and upper trunk
src.explanation: The cause is incompletely understood, but dysbiosis, altered immunity and barrier dysfunction contribute, in sebaceous-rich scalp, face and upper trunk.

items.section_title: 4.2 · Objectives d & e — Globe shape, and the age-related conditions
items.html: Presbyopia. The lens stiffens and the ciliary muscle loses accommodation, through sclerosis, so the eye can no longer focus on near objects.

src.question: What is the mechanism of presbyopia?
src.key: The lens stiffens and the ciliary muscle loses accommodation, through sclerosis
src.explanation: Correct — sclerosis stiffens the lens and the ciliary muscle loses accommodation, so the eye can no longer focus on near objects.

items.section_title: 5.8 · Rhinology
items.html: Posterior versus anterior epistaxis. Posterior bleeds reflect systemic causes. Anterior causes are local insults to the mucosa; posterior causes act on the vessels and on clotting.

src.question: Why does anticoagulation favor POSTERIOR rather than anterior epistaxis?
src.key: Posterior bleeds reflect systemic causes
src.explanation: Anterior causes are local insults to the mucosa; posterior causes act on the vessels and on clotting.
